Per-sample CNV_HIGH counts are mostly single-digit (0-22 cells) for a reliable prevalence estimate. Best described as an observed CNV-like score shift with an ambiguous, nonconfirmatory signal -- not attributable with this method to CNV vs. lineage-driven expression differences (epithelial vs immune) vs. resolution loss, treated as co-equal, un-excluded explanations.
notes: This does NOT confirm malignancy at the single-cell level and does NOT supersede or strengthen TE004/TE005 (the epithelial-proxy screen) -- TE004/TE005 remain Module B's primary evidence for this target. Recorded as its own honestly-characterized attempt: an observed, modest, population-level CNV-like score shift, directionally consistent with malignancy but ambiguous and nonconfirmatory at the single-cell level. This coarse arm-level method lacks within-cell gene-order smoothing and a centering/reference-subtraction step (not primarily "no cross-cell smoothing"), and its mean(z^2) aggregate erases gain/loss direction; lineage-driven expression differences (epithelial vs immune, unrelated to copy number) are an equally plausible, co-equal alternative explanation for the shift, not a secondary caveat. Reference and epithelial-proxy populations are restricted to the 3 treated patients (COL15/COL17/COL18), matching TE004's indication_id=mcrc_preop_chemotherapy_crlm -- a round-3 fix (PR #75 round-2 review) after an earlier version pooled all 6 GSE178318 patients (82% treatment-naive) under this treated-cohort row; the pooled-population numbers are kept only as a method diagnostic in the analysis contract.
